title: He’s better than Polonius though #shakespeare #hamlet #fathersday #th...
transcript: I'm gonna rank every piece of advice that Polonius gives in his speech to Laertes in hamlet in honor of Father's Day. In last place, I have, Essentially saying, try not to get into a fight, but if you're already in a fight, make sure you win. I feel like the second part of that kinda undermines the first. Like, maybe we just shouldn't get into fights. It certainly didn't work out very well for Laertes. Next, I have You know, this is very, uh, rich people coded advice, but not bad. It's true that it's kinda tacky to flaunt your expensive clothes, and obviously this whole clothes make the man thing is, like, a popular piece of advice, but, you know, I feel like it's less and less applicable these days. Uh, fine. It's a little vague. Next. Yeah, this is decent advice. It's good to stay out of debt. And it's true that, you know, lending money to friends can get complicated, but this one kinda depends on the situation, right? Like, never borrow or lend money? Then Polonius has like three different ways of saying, “keep your mouth shut.” He says, This one, I guess more about being like a good listener. This one's more about giving and receiving opinions This one, I guess, is more about having a filter. The second best piece of advice in this speech is, Essentially saying, when you have friends who have proven themselves to be true and good friends, you better hang on to ‘em And just cause you're hanging out and having fun with someone new doesn't automatically mean that they're a trustworthy friend. But of course, in first place, this above all, to thine own self be true. Great advice for all of us. And a happy Father's Day to my very own Polonius.
